back_translation: In the ninth year, in the tenth month, on the tenth day of the month, the word of the LORD came to me, saying,
“Son of man, write down this day, this very day, for on this very day the king of Babylon has begun to besiege Jerusalem.
Speak a parable to this rebellious house and tell them, the Lord GOD says this: Set the pot on; set it on, and pour water into it.
Put in the pieces of meat, every good piece—the thigh and the shoulder—fill it with choice bones.
Take the best of the flock and pile the wood beneath it; bring it to a rolling boil and cook the bones in it too.’
Therefore the Lord GOD says this: Woe to the city of bloodshed, to the pot that has rusted, whose rust cannot be scraped off! Take the meat out piece by piece, without casting lots to choose.
For the blood she shed is still within her; she poured it out on bare rock; she did not pour it on the ground to cover it with dust.
To stir up wrath and to take vengeance, I have set her blood on the bare rock, so that it would not be covered.
Therefore the Lord GOD says this: Woe to the city of bloodshed! I Myself will make the pile of wood great.
Pile on much wood, kindle the fire, cook the meat thoroughly, season it with spices, and let the bones be charred.
Then set the empty pot on its coals so that it becomes hot and its copper glows red, so that its impurity may be melted within it and its rust be burned away completely.
It has worn out every effort in vain; its thick rust still cannot be scraped off, even by the fire.
In your uncleanness there is lewdness. Because I tried to cleanse you but you would not be cleansed from your uncleanness, you will not be cleansed again until I have fully spent My wrath upon you.

I, the LORD, have spoken; it will come, and I will act. I will not hold back, I will not show pity, and I will not relent. They will judge you according to your ways and your deeds, declares the Lord GOD.”
Then the word of the LORD came to me, saying,
“Son of man, behold, I am about to take away the desire of your eyes from you with a single blow; but you must not mourn or weep, and do not let your tears flow.
Groan quietly; do not hold a mourning rite for the dead. Bind your turban on your head and put your sandals on your feet; do not cover your lips or eat the bread of mourners.”
So I spoke to the people in the morning, and in the evening my wife died. The next morning I did as I had been commanded.
Then the people asked me, “Will you not tell us what these things you are doing mean for us?”
So I answered them, “The word of the LORD came to me, saying,

Say to the house of Israel, the Lord GOD says this: Behold, I am about to defile My sanctuary, the pride of your power, the desire of your eyes, and the delight your soul cherishes; and the sons and daughters you left behind will fall by the sword.
Then you will do as I have done: you will not cover your lips or eat the bread of mourners.
Your turbans will remain on your heads and your sandals on your feet. You will not mourn or weep, but you will waste away because of your iniquities and groan to one another.
So Ezekiel will be a sign to you; you will do everything just as he has done. When this comes, you will know that I am the Lord GOD.’
And you, son of man, on the day I take away from them their stronghold, their joy and their glory, the desire of their eyes and the longing of their souls—their sons and daughters too—
on that day a fugitive will come to you to bring the news to your ears.
On that day your mouth will be opened when you meet the fugitive; you will speak and no longer be mute. So you will be a sign to them, and they will know that I am the LORD.”
